extracted.intended_audience: poets, fiction writers, and readers interested in The Kenyon Review (potential submitters and general audience)
extracted.subtask_description: Information about The Kenyon Review's publication history, editorial practices, and specific eligibility/selection rules relevant to poets and short-fiction writers considering submission or awards. Includes procedural details on poetry reading and eligibility for the Short Fiction Prize and the Kenyon Review Award for Literary Achievement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry submissions — volume and publication rates
rubrics_metrics.description: The magazine receives over 3,000 submissions a year (batches, not individual poems), and publishes some 50 of them per year in the print version, another 25 in the annual "Nature's Nature" feature; more poems are published in the Kenyon Review Online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This gives an implied acceptance-rate benchmark (roughly 50–75 print-feature acceptances out of ~3,000 submission batches) and distinguishes solicited vs. open-submission slots in estimating chances of publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry submissions — solicitation vs open submissions and selection workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: Of the poems published, perhaps 15 or 20 are solicited, so around 60 come via the open submission route. A group of trained student associates do part of the first reading and they have the right to reject; it takes two such rejections before a poem is actually rejected. David Baker does the final selection, and David Lynn does the "final sign-off."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is multi-stage: student associates perform initial triage (each with veto power that requires two rejections to eliminate a poem), then the poetry editor (Baker) selects, followed by final editorial sign-off. Solicited work has a substantial share of slots, reducing the open-submission share.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kenyon Review Short Fiction Prize — eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The Kenyon Review Short Fiction Prize, established in 2008, is awarded annually to a writer who has not previously published a work of fiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility is limited to previously unpublished fiction writers (i.e., those who have not published a work of fiction). The prize is a contest-specific criterion distinguishing emerging/unpublished authors from established authors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kenyon Review Award for Literary Achievement — selection values
rubrics_metrics.description: The "Kenyon Review Award for Literary Achievement" was created to honor careers of extraordinary literary achievement, recognizing writers whose influence and importance have shaped the American literary landscape. It celebrates writers for the courage of their vision, their unparalleled imagination, and for the beauty of their art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Award selection emphasizes lifetime/career-level impact, influence on the American literary landscape, courage of vision, imagination, and aesthetic excellence. The award is intended to honor exceptional, influential careers rather than single works.
